pluss::note::full_bytes_like¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::full_bytes_like(const Note& like, string_view value)

Borrow A Shape, Fill It In Bytes Mode¶

full_bytes_like() is full_like with a bytes-mode result: it takes the shape of an existing Note and returns a fresh bytes-mode Note (encoding=bytes) of that shape, with value copied into every cell.

This is the shape-first way into bytes mode. There is deliberately no free-standing full_bytes(sizes, value) factory — when you want a bytes block of a known geometry, you almost always have a Note of that geometry already (the text you are about to re-tag, mask, or pair with a binary column), so the shape is borrowed rather than restated. If you truly have only a sizes list, pass it to bytes with a flat cell range.

As with full_like, only the shape of like is read; its contents and its own encoding do not matter. value is stored as raw bytes with no UTF-8 validation — that is the whole point of bytes mode. Print the result with opt.bytes_mode = pluss::NotePrintBytesMode::Hex when the content is not mostly printable ASCII.

like must be a defined Note. The result is independent of like.

Example 1: A Bytes Block Shaped Like An Existing Note¶

pluss::NotePrintOptions hex;
hex.bytes_mode = pluss::NotePrintBytesMode::Hex;

const auto grid = pluss::note::make({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::full_bytes_like(grid, "\xDE\xAD"), hex)
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=bytes)
[
  [hex[de ad], hex[de ad], hex[de ad]], 
  [hex[de ad], hex[de ad], hex[de ad]]
]

Shape [2, 3] came from grid; every cell holds the two raw bytes DE AD, and the Note is in bytes mode.
